solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cook apple and fry stick insects with it

indicators.note: to cook something is to work on it, so the letters of the following words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe that oddly tells you to fry apple alongside stick insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges APPLE and FRY together. 'Stick insects' looks like the creature, but here it means to glue bugs in place, which is what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky paper hung up to trap flies and other bugs is the thing you glue insects with.

clue.text: Odd lot missing from tall order being arranged in storeroom

indicators.note: being arranged means the letters of tall order are rearranged once lot is taken out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some lot is absent from a tall order now being sorted into the stockroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' signals that LOT's letters are scattered, and 'missing from' takes them out of TALL ORDER; 'being arranged' shuffles the remaining ALRDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry where food is kept is a kind of storeroom.

clue.text: To important person on the way up it's the turning-point

indicators.note: on the way up, in a down clue, means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A celebrity's rise is the turning-point of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the fixed point on which something turns, so a turning-point literally.

clue.text: Loyal Irishman's nervous reaction, imbibing port

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the port is taken inside

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A faithful Irishman twitches nervously while drinking port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine to go with 'imbibing'; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted to one's country, hence loyal; a near-synonym.

clue.text: Sir sent back German dish

indicators.note: sent back means the word Sir is reversed

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A knight returns a German meal to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice preparation, an example of a dish.

clue.text: Be put back in charge to get refund

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the word for charge

parts.note: a charge is a rate, the price asked

indicators.note: put back tells us the word be is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone restored to a post of responsibility in order to get money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests being responsible for something; here it is a price. 'put back' reverses the first word, and 'in' sets it inside the price.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial repayment of money already paid is a refund, a synonym in finance.

clue.text: Make a response to 'Play it again'?

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to play a part is to act

explanation.surface: A request to perform the piece once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link word; to act again is to RE-ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to something is to react to it; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Do for vegetarians?

parts.note: a do is a party; a feast of beans would suit vegetarians

explanation.definitionFit: A jolly celebration or party, punningly a meal of pulses for non-meat-eaters.

clue.text: Deter reshuffles after support for course seesawed

indicators.note: after places the shuffled word behind the golf support

parts.note: on a golf course the ball is supported on a tee

indicators.note: reshuffles means the letters of deter are rearranged

explanation.surface: Deterrent reshuffles after course support caused wavering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a race or meal course; here it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocked unsteadily back and forth, as a seesaw does.

clue.text: Hedge sparrow's second character with rook I scrutinise

indicators.note: second character picks the second letter of the bird's name

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook
to vet is to scrutinise or examine closely

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher studies a hedge sparrow and a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hedge sparrow' reads as the bird (the dunnock), but 'Hedge' is the definition and 'sparrow' supplies its second letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A common evergreen shrub used for garden boundaries, so an example of a hedge plant.

clue.text: Mariner's fears are misplaced

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters are put in the wrong places, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor's anxieties are unfounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor or seagoing traveller; both words name someone who goes to sea.

clue.text: Confine engineers near stern

indicators.note: near places the first piece next to the second, side by side

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
stern and strict are synonyms for severe

explanation.surface: An order to keep engineers close to the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' suggests the rear of a boat; here it is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit or keep within bounds; a verb synonym for confining.

clue.text: Clump thug in audience with iron before end of act

indicators.note: before puts the iron piece ahead of the final letter
in audience means as heard by listeners, so the word for thug is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tough is a thug or rough
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word act

explanation.surface: Thump a ruffian in the theatre audience with a golf iron before the act finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clump' looks like a verb to hit, matching 'thug'; it is a noun, a tuft of grass. TUF is how TOUGH is said; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mound or tuft of grass, as in the nursery rhyme, so a clump of vegetation.

clue.text: Artist doing nudes? The underwear could go here

definitions.meaning: a chest drawer at the base, where clothes or a bride's linen are kept

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a pun: a painter of nudes draws rear ends. The second is literal: the lowest drawer of a chest, traditionally where a bride-to-be stores linen.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest drawer of a chest, traditionally for a bride's linen; jokingly, a sketcher of rear ends.

clue.text: Bishop is missing pasty — a rare bird!

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
lacks means is missing or is without
pasty and wan both mean pale

explanation.surface: A pale bishop is absent: what a rarity!
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like a pie; it is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-plumaged swan was once thought impossible, so the phrase means a rarity, idiomatically.

clue.text: Severe steward — I will be ejected in mid-ocean perhaps

parts.note: deep as in severe, as in deep trouble

indicators.note: will be ejected means the letter I is thrown out of the waiter

parts.note: a steward serving food is a waiter

explanation.surface: A stern steward announces that he will be thrown out in the middle of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea far from shore has great depth, so mid-ocean is an example.

clue.text: Extravagant faults we disguised

indicators.note: disguised means the letters are concealed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: We hide our failings behind lavish spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending too freely, so prodigal or extravagant; synonyms.

clue.text: Surplus with these revised accounts

parts.note: a balance is a surplus or remainder

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note that the surplus figure goes with these corrected accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of a company's assets and liabilities is a form of financial accounts.

clue.text: Fancy panties — is that wise?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Would buying frilly underwear be a sensible idea?
explanation.walkthrough: 'is that' joins the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having great wisdom or discernment; a literary synonym.

clue.text: Not immediately obvious it is discarded from secondary name

indicators.note: is discarded from means the word it is taken out

parts.note: a subtitle is a secondary title or name

explanation.surface: Something hidden: it is dropped from a backup name.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate and hard to notice, so not obvious at once.

clue.text: Bet spades draw with diamonds

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
a draw, the money a show attracts, is its take
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player wagers on spades and draws to diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game surface makes 'draw' look like taking a card; it means takings.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of staking: wagered money, synonymous with having bet.

clue.text: One degree Celsius in river in thaw

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
the Roman numeral I is one
C is the abbreviation for degrees Celsius

explanation.surface: Water at one degree in a river is starting to thaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove ice from something is to thaw it out; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Energy being interrupted, might stop filming

definitions.meaning: a failure of the electricity supply
a blackout on set would halt shooting, and 'cut' is what a director calls

explanation.definitionFit: An outage of electricity supply interrupts energy, and would halt any film shoot.

clue.text: Majestic delight unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to regale is to delight or entertain

explanation.surface: Royal pleasure cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal and stately, so majestic; synonyms.

clue.text: Not wanting light cream

parts.note: to be off something is to have lost one's appetite for it
light as in pale, as in light or white coffee

explanation.surface: Declining a pale cream offered in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' looks like the dairy product but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is a pale yellowish shade, a near-white colour.

clue.text: The alternative to slacks!

parts.note: slacks are loose trousers; the opposite of slack is taut, and the clinging legwear is the alternative garment

explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting legwear garment worn instead of trousers, and taut is the opposite of slack.

clue.text: Look to make a cricket score?

definitions.meaning: a cricket stroke deflecting the ball fine with an angled bat, scoring runs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a glance is a stroke that deflects the ball fine past the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief look, and also a cricket shot deflecting the ball off the bat's face for runs.

clue.text: Excited seeing the daughter crossing brook

indicators.note: crossing means the first pieces span across the brook, enclosing it

parts.note: a rill is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: A girl is delighted as she wades over a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' means the definite article plus the daughter's letter straddle the stream's name, as a bridge spans a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted and excited are synonyms for feeling a rush of pleasure.
